title: Directed contact-stack stability diverges by mass placement at 32:1 and contact presence cannot certify load transmission
claim: For the exact L1.7 fixed-total-2-kg two-box contact stack at 60 Hz across a neutral 1:1 cell and directed ratios 2:1 through 1024:1 in both orientations, physical gates admit heavy-on-top through 16:1 and first reject it at the measured 32:1, while every measured heavy-on-bottom cell through 1024:1 passes; the two directions first diverge at 32:1 and fresh-world repeats reproduce all three boundary classifications. Floor and pair contact fractions stayed 1.0 even in grossly unstable top-heavy cells, and the raw floor impulse tracked the bottom body's own weight rather than the transmitted stack load, for example approximately 0.0215 N raw against approximately 19.667 N reconstructed at top-heavy 1024:1.
scope: Two unjointed stacked boxes with fixed total mass 2 kg, masses m_light = M/(1+r) and m_heavy = M*r/(1+r), both stack orientations, 60 Hz Jolt physics, Godot 4.7, fresh SubViewport world per cell with a tagged excluded activation warm-up tick, physical-metric classification with interpolation forbidden.
mechanism: The iterative contact solver resolves a heavy body supported by a light one less robustly than the reverse at equal total mass, producing a direction-dependent stability envelope. Contact presence only proves geometric touching; pose, momentum, and load-transmission metrics detect failure that presence misses, and the raw local floor impulse reports the bottom body's local transmission rather than the whole-stack support load.
applicability: Bounding unjointed contact-stack mass ratios for lab fixture design
Demonstrating that contact-presence checks are insufficient stability evidence
failure_boundaries: Does not cover articulated parent/child mass ratios; joints are deferred until L2 joint truth exists
Does not cover unmeasured ratios between grid cells; interpolation is forbidden
Does not bound the heavy-on-bottom direction beyond the measured 1024:1 endpoint, which remains open
Does not establish standing, bracing, fall arrest, getting up, or walking

minimal_repair_rules.symptom: A top-heavy unjointed contact stack destabilizes while all contact-presence checks stay green
minimal_repair_rules.diagnosis: The mass ratio sits beyond the measured top-heavy envelope and presence metrics cannot see the failure
minimal_repair_rules.smallest_change: Keep top-heavy contact-stack ratios at or below the measured 16:1 cell or place the heavy body on the bottom
minimal_repair_rules.expected_effect: Pose, momentum, and load-transmission metrics return inside the measured accepted class
do_not_apply_when: The stack is articulated or jointed rather than pure contact
